sections.heading: C — Driving records, suspensions and reinstatement
sections.markdown:
## C — Driving records, suspensions and reinstatement

FACT_ID: sec15-F01 | anchor: A122
Careless driving or certain law violations can lead to suspension, cancellation or revocation even before a person has received a license. [A122]
Source: [A122 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0122]

FACT_ID: sec15-F02 | anchor: A122
Idaho maintains crash and moving-violation records, including out-of-state events, for people who have never received a license as well as licensed drivers. [A122]
Source: [A122 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0122]

FACT_ID: sec15-F03 | anchor: A122
The handbook identifies Idaho as a Driver License Compact member and describes the compact as promoting compliance across member states. [A122]
Source: [A122 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0122]

FACT_ID: sec15-F04 | anchor: A122
Under the described compact, serious offenses and minor moving violations go to the driver's home state for treatment as a home-state violation. [A122]
Source: [A122 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0122]

FACT_ID: sec15-F05 | anchor: A122
A licensed Idaho driver's out-of-state traffic conviction is added to the Idaho record, with suspension if the offense is suspendable. [A122]
Source: [A122 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0122]

FACT_ID: sec15-F06 | anchor: A123
The handbook's moving-violation point scale assigns one through four points per recorded violation. [A123]
Source: [A123 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0123]

FACT_ID: sec15-F07 | anchor: A123
The point table lists a warning letter for eight through eleven points within any twelve months. [A123]
Source: [A123 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0123]

FACT_ID: sec15-F08 | anchor: A123
The point table lists a thirty-day suspension for twelve through seventeen points within any twelve months. [A123]
Source: [A123 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0123]

FACT_ID: sec15-F09 | anchor: A123
The point table lists a ninety-day suspension for eighteen through twenty-three points within any twenty-four months. [A123]
Source: [A123 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0123]

FACT_ID: sec15-F10 | anchor: A123
The point table lists a six-month suspension for at least twenty-four points within any thirty-six months. [A123]
Source: [A123 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0123]

FACT_ID: sec15-F11 | anchor: A123
The handbook permits point removal once in three years through an approved defensive-driving course or the described law-enforcement traffic course. [A123]
Source: [A123 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0123]

FACT_ID: sec15-F12 | anchor: A123
Those point-removal courses reduce points but do not remove the conviction from the driving record. [A123]
Source: [A123 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0123]

FACT_ID: sec15-F13 | anchor: A123
Completing an ITD-approved defensive-driving course can remove at most three points, and the points must already be recorded before the course is completed. [A123]
Source: [A123 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0123]

FACT_ID: sec15-F14 | anchor: A124
The handbook authorizes courts and the department to impose several license actions for listed convictions; its list is not exhaustive. [A124]
Source: [A124 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0124]

FACT_ID: sec15-F15 | anchor: A124
Driving under the influence, using a vehicle for a felony and reckless driving appear among the listed license-action grounds. [A124]
Source: [A124 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0124]

FACT_ID: sec15-F16 | anchor: A124
Leaving an involved crash with property damage, injury or death appears among the listed license-action grounds. [A124]
Source: [A124 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0124]

FACT_ID: sec15-F17 | anchor: A124
False oral or written statements under oath to the department are a listed license-action ground. [A124]
Source: [A124 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0124]

FACT_ID: sec15-F18 | anchor: A124
An unpaid crash-damages judgment, an evidentiary-test failure or refusal, and fleeing an officer appear among the listed grounds. [A124]
Source: [A124 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0124]

FACT_ID: sec15-F19 | anchor: A124
Unlawful license or identification-card use, lack of required vehicle insurance and violating a license restriction appear among the listed grounds. [A124]
Source: [A124 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0124]

FACT_ID: sec15-F20 | anchor: A124
The source also lists school-compliance failures, unpaid child support, visitation noncompliance and failure to obey a paternity-suit subpoena. [A124]
Source: [A124 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0124]

FACT_ID: sec15-F21 | anchor: A125
For drivers younger than seventeen, the first moving-violation conviction brings the handbook's warning letter. [A125]
Source: [A125 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0125]

FACT_ID: sec15-F22 | anchor: A125
For drivers younger than seventeen, a second moving-violation conviction carries a thirty-day driving suspension. [A125]
Source: [A125 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0125]

FACT_ID: sec15-F23 | anchor: A125
For drivers younger than seventeen, a third or later moving-violation conviction carries a sixty-day suspension. [A125]
Source: [A125 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0125]

FACT_ID: sec15-F24 | anchor: A125
The described GDL penalties are additional to supervised-instruction permit cancellation or other court or department suspensions. [A125]
Source: [A125 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0125]

FACT_ID: sec15-F25 | anchor: A125
The GDL penalty periods are absolute and allow no driving privileges of any kind. [A125]
Source: [A125 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0125]

FACT_ID: sec15-F26 | anchor: A125
After a DUI arrest and an evidentiary result over the legal alcohol limit, an officer serves an immediate suspension notice; a notice may instead be sent after blood or urine results establish the described intoxication. [A125]
Source: [A125 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0125]

FACT_ID: sec15-F27 | anchor: A125
The described ALS is an administrative suspension imposed by the transportation department under the cited alcohol-test law. [A125]
Source: [A125 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0125]

FACT_ID: sec15-F28 | anchor: A125
The handbook allows an ALS hearing request within seven days of the date written on the suspension notice, before a department-designated hearing officer. [A125]
Source: [A125 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0125]

Misconceptions: Removing points does not erase a conviction. An administrative suspension is separate from criminal proceedings. A restricted permit is possible only when eligible, not an automatic exception to an absolute suspension.
Mnemonic: Trigger, period and permission is a learning cue for comparing the supported consequence rules.
Glossary: ALS means administrative license suspension; an absolute suspension permits no driving; an ignition interlock checks a breath sample before engine starting.
Dynamic facts: sanctions, monetary amounts, course availability and reinstatement channels are source-described and remain blocked for current legal verification.

verification_debt.claim_text: All driving-record, point, GDL and suspension consequences in these mapped pages are source descriptions from the staged handbook. Current statutory scope, exceptions and amendments have not passed the reserved legal review; current-law release remains blocked.

The Traffic Safety Education Course rule begins on physical page one hundred twenty-three and continues onto one hundred twenty-four. Its full conditions include a maximum four-point reduction, an officer's offer and driver acceptance at citation, completion within forty-five days and removal tied to that citation's points. The complete multi-page rule is withheld rather than omitting its deadline.

The handbook's approved-course website, contact number and current local Traffic Safety Education Course availability were not checked. No present approval, provider access or appointment is promised.
